keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (no Cliopatria row). 'Established: 147 BC'; Kamnaskires I Soter (c. 147 BC?) and Kamnaskires II Nikephoros (c. 147-139 BC) rule the autonomous kingdom. The page gives no area or boundary; the gazetteer's Khuzestan (about 66,000 km2) is the reading of 'Susiana, the present-day Khuzestan'. The page names three provinces (Massabatice, later Masabadhan; Corbiane; Gabiane) without placing them. [Added after review me-06-x, 2026-10-19: this shape (Khuzestan, about 66,300 km2) overlaps the Cliopatria Seleucid Empire shape seleucid-empire_-164 (alive to -145) on 248 cells (about 62,700 km2) for -147 to -145, and the seleucid-empire ledger has no loss of Susiana to Elymais between -164 and -141. The Elymais page gives 147 BC as the establishment date ('Established: 147 BC', Kamnaskires I Soter 'c. 147 BC ?') but nothing on Seleucid rule of Susa before it, so the overlap stands as the page's own date against Cliopatria's -145; the loss is routed to the seleucid-empire gap-filler.]

correction.text: Khuzestan again under its own Kamnaskirid kings: Kamnaskires III and Anzaze c. 82-62/61 BC (coins attested 82-75 BC), Kamnaskires IV and V in the 1st century BC, Kamnaskires VI in the mid/late 1st century AD, Orodes V in 221/222

ledger.note: 147 BC: Kamnaskires I Soter founds the kingdom of Elymais in Susiana. Elymais infobox 'Established: 147 BC, preceded by the Seleucid Empire'; the king list has Kamnaskires I Soter c. 147 BC (with a question mark) and Kamnaskires II Nikephoros c. 147-139 BC. Elymaeans had already killed Antiochus III in 187 BC after he pillaged the temple of Bel.

ledger.note: c. 82 BC: the restored kingdom of Elymais is a Parthian vassal. Elymais page (re-read 2026-10-19): the kingdom was 'frequently a vassal under Parthian control' (intro); infobox status 'Autonomous state, frequently a vassal of the Parthian Empire'; 'From 140/139 BC, Elymais was then under direct Parthian control for several decades ... until around 82 BC'. The page does not say the vassalage was continuous or give a year for each change of status ('frequently'), so the tint runs from the restoration at -82 to the end; the year is the page's 'around 82 BC' and the region is the whole kingdom. Mirrors the parthian-empire vassal_start for elymais, which has -140 (direct control, not a vassal tint, according to this page). [Added after review me-06-x, 2026-10-19]

wars.outcome: Elymais passed under direct Parthian control for several decades; Mithridates I's forces occupied Susa.

The Mithridates I page has 'conquered Elymais in 140/139 BC' (a modern identification of a relief, now disputed) and a second punitive invasion after Elymais aided Demetrius II, undated.

wars.outcome: Occasional rebellions until about 82 BC; then Kamnaskires III and Anzaze rule a vassal Elymais.
wars.note: Elymais page: 'Occasional rebellions occurred until about 82 BC'. Shayegan, cited there, speculates that Kamnaskires III and Anzaze were later replaced by the Parthians after dealings with Pompey in 62/61 BC. Antiochus VII occupied Susa in 130 BC (Parthian Empire page); the Elymais page says Susa lay east of Elymais, so that episode is not entered as an Elymaean loss.

wars.note: The date range is the infobox's 221/222; the Ardashir I page gives no year for killing the governor of Susa. The parthian-empire dossier dates the end of the Elymais vassalage to 224.

notes:
State Cliopatria lacks (new_slug elymais), listed as needed by the me-06-a and me-06-c reports. Pages opened: Elymais, Parthian Empire, Mithridates I of Parthia, Ardashir I. The Kamnaskirid dynasty page did not load (URL_NOT_FOUND) and the Hyspaosines page was not used for Elymais beyond a letter about 'Mithridates II's defeat of Elymais' which it does not date.

STATUS DISAGREEMENT: the Elymais page says 'direct Parthian control' from 140/139 to about 82 BC; the parthian-empire dossier carries a vassal_start for elymais at -140 and a vassal_end at 224. For -140 to -83 the Parthian land should be drawn plain (or hatched, rule 4), not as a lighter vassal tint, and the Elymais dossier draws nothing there. From -82 the page says 'frequently a vassal'. End year: this dossier uses the infobox's 221/222 (222); the parthian-empire dossier uses 224.

Unsettled: the capital (the infobox says Susa; the text says Susa lay east of Elymais); the provinces Massabatice, Corbiane and Gabiane are not placed on the page (a gazetteer/gap-filler task); the Luristan uplands, Elymais in the Greek sources, are not claimed because the page does not mention them. Dating of the early kings (Okkonapses 188-187 BC per Rezakhani; Kamnaskires the Soter 133-130 BC per Shayegan) is disputed on the page. No rulers strip. Gazetteer: all names resolve.

REPAIR 2026-10-19 (author, after review me-06-x): (1) Added vassal_start at -82 (after the gain) and vassal_end at 222 (before the dissolve), counterpart parthian-empire, region Khuzestan, confidence 2 (the reviewer's blocking finding). Elymais page re-read: 'frequently a vassal under Parthian control'; infobox status 'Autonomous state, frequently a vassal of the Parthian Empire'; 'From 140/139 BC, Elymais was then under direct Parthian control for several decades ... until around 82 BC'. ROUTE TO parthian-empire (me-06-a): turn its -140 vassal_start for elymais into a gain of Khuzestan (direct rule -140 to -83; the page says 'direct Parthian control'), add a -82 loss to elymais plus a vassal_start (this dossier mirrors it), and move the vassal_end from 224 to 222 (or note the two-year difference). The page does not date the individual changes of status that 'frequently' implies, so one vassal span -82 to 222 is the reading. (2) ROUTE TO seleucid-empire (me-05): a loss of Khuzestan to elymais in -147 (Cliopatria's Seleucid shape holds it to -145; see the keyframe note). I do not change the Elymais start: the page's date is 147 BC. (3) Thin item, the royal seat: the Elymais page was re-read; it names only Susa (infobox) and says 'Susa lay to the east of the territory of Elymais', and no other seat. The Seleucia on the Hedyphon page was tried twice (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seleucia_on_the_Hedyphon and, as a redirect guess, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seleucia_on_the_Hedypnus) and did not load (URL_NOT_FOUND), so the capital stays Susa with its caveat; no unsourced seat is entered. (4) Thin item, the provinces: the Elymais page lists 'Massabatice (later Masabadhan), Corbiane and Gabiane' and does not place them ('Susa lay to the east of the territory of Elymais'); the provinces cannot be drawn from this page, so the keyframe stays Khuzestan, still a gazetteer/gap-filler task.
